# Platforms

<!-- Generated by `kaleidophone platforms --markdown` from src/kaleidophone/render/platforms.py.
     Don't edit it by hand: change the registry, then regenerate. tests/test_platforms.py fails
     when this file is out of date. -->

What each platform asks for, as `kaleidophone deliver` delivers to it and
`kaleidophone platforms` prints it. Every number is **cited**: each entry
lists its sources -- the platform's own documentation where it publishes
any -- its confidence (`official`: the platform's own pages or API reference;
`third-party`: guides, press or measurements, because the platform publishes
nothing) and the date it was checked. Platforms change these without notice:
check the date before you trust one.

Where the sources disagree, the safe value is the hard limit and the rest
is in the notes. **Length** and **file limit** are the most the platform
takes -- a delivery sheet that asks for more is refused; in brackets, where
`deliver` starts warning, and why is under the entry. **Loudness** is the
level the platform plays audio at; `deliver` reports how far each delivered
file sits from it.

kaleidophone makes the files and stops there: nothing here talks to a
platform ([ADR-0006](decisions/0006-the-release-pack.md)).

## instagram-reel

**Instagram Reel** (video); also `ig-reel`

- **size:** 1080x1920 (9:16); at most 1920 px wide
- **length:** 3 s to 15 min; warns over 3 min: Instagram recommends Reels under 3 min to reach non-followers; up to 15 min is allowed (20 min from the app's camera since Nov 2025)
- **frame rate:** 23-60 (Graph API range); 30 typical
- **audio:** optional
- **file:** at most 300 MB
- **safe area:** keep clear of top 269, bottom 672, left 65, right 65 px
- **formats:** mp4, mov
- **codec:** H.264 or HEVC, progressive, closed GOP, 4:2:0, VBR <=25 Mbps, <=1920 px wide; AAC <=48 kHz mono/stereo, 128 kbps; moov atom at front, no edit lists (Graph API reel spec).
- **notes:** Max length is disputed. Sep-2026 third-party guides and Instagram's own in-app camera update (Nov 2025) say 20 min. The help-centre meta description still says 'up to 3 minutes'. The Graph API allows 15 min / 300 MB. Instagram only recommends Reels under 3 min to non-followers. 300 MB is the API cap; the in-app cap is unpublished (Meta ads guide: 4 GB). Safe area is Meta ads-guide wording: 'at least 14% of the top, 35% of the bottom and 6% on each side' (read via a third-party quote because facebook.com is robots-blocked).
- **confidence:** third-party, checked 2026-09-30

## instagram-reel-cover

**Instagram Reel cover** (image); also `ig-reel-cover`

- **size:** 1080x1920 (9:16)
- **audio:** none
- **file:** no limit published
- **safe area:** keep clear of top 240, bottom 240, left 0, right 0 px
- **formats:** jpg
- **codec:** sRGB JPEG. The Graph API cover_url sets the Reels-tab cover. API images are capped at 8 MB (assumed to apply to covers too).
- **notes:** Shown at full 9:16 in the Reels tab. The profile grid shows the centre 3:4 (1080x1440), so keep titles and faces inside the middle 1440 px. Since early 2026 you can reposition the grid crop after posting with 'Adjust preview'.

## instagram-grid-thumbnail

**Instagram profile grid tile** (image); also `ig-grid`, `ig-grid-thumbnail`

- **size:** 1080x1440 (3:4)
- **audio:** none
- **file:** no limit published
- **formats:** none: not an upload
- **codec:** A display crop, not an upload.
- **notes:** Grid tiles changed from 1:1 to 3:4 in Jan 2025 and are still 3:4 in Sep-2026 guides. Centre-crop maths: a 9:16 cover shows its middle 1080x1440 (240 px lost top and bottom); a 4:5 post shows ~1012x1350 (34 px lost each side); a 1:1 post shows 810x1080 (135 px lost each side); a 3:4 post is uncropped. The crop can be adjusted per post with 'Adjust preview' (~Mar 2026).
- **confidence:** third-party, checked 2026-09-30

## instagram-story

**Instagram Story** (video); also `ig-story`

- **size:** 1080x1920 (9:16); at most 1920 px wide
- **length:** 3 s to 1 min
- **frame rate:** 23-60
- **audio:** optional
- **file:** at most 100 MB
- **safe area:** keep clear of top 269, bottom 672, left 65, right 65 px
- **formats:** mp4, mov, jpg
- **codec:** Same video rules as Reels (H.264/HEVC, AAC <=48 kHz, VBR <=25 Mbps, <=1920 px). Story images: JPEG <=8 MB, sRGB.
- **notes:** 60 s per story card, confirmed by Instagram in Sep 2022; third parties say longer uploads are split into cards. The safe area uses Meta's 9:16 guidance for Stories and Reels, which a third party reports was unified in Mar 2026. The older Stories-only guidance was ~14% top and ~20% (384 px) bottom. The safe area is third-party.
- **confidence:** official, checked 2026-09-30

## instagram-carousel-image

**Instagram carousel image** (image); also `ig-carousel`, `ig-carousel-image`

- **size:** 1080x1440 (3:4; allowed 1.91:1 to 3:4; 1:1 and 4:5 also common); also 1080x1350, 1080x1080, 1080x566; 320 to 1440 px wide
- **audio:** none
- **file:** at most 8 MB
- **formats:** jpg
- **codec:** Graph API: JPEG only, sRGB, 320-1440 px wide, ratio 4:5 to 1.91:1 (the API has not added 3:4). The app displays images 1080 px wide.
- **notes:** Up to 20 photos or videos per post in the app (was 10 until Aug 2024; the Graph API is still 10). 3:4 portrait has been allowed in the app since 29 May 2025 (the previous maximum was 4:5, 1080x1350). Third parties say the first slide sets the frame, so design all slides at one ratio. Also applies to single-image feed posts.

## tiktok

**TikTok** (video); also `tt`

- **size:** 1080x1920 (9:16); each side 360 to 4096 px
- **length:** up to 10 min; warns over 3 min: every TikTok creator can post 3 min; only some can post 5 or 10
- **frame rate:** 23-60
- **audio:** optional
- **file:** at most 4096 MB; warns over 72 MB: third parties report ~72 MB as the Android app's cap (~287.6 MB on iOS); the API takes 4096 MB
- **safe area:** keep clear of top 130, bottom 484, left 44, right 140 px
- **formats:** mp4, webm, mov
- **codec:** H.264 recommended (H.265, VP8 and VP9 accepted); each side 360-4096 px (Content Posting API).
- **notes:** TikTok's own doc: 'All TikTok creators can post 3-minute videos, while some have access to post 5-minute or 10-minute videos.' Only 180 s is guaranteed; the API maximum is 600 s. 60-min web uploads were a limited 2024 test. 4 GB is the API cap. The in-app caps (~287.6 MB iOS, ~72 MB Android) and ~10 GB on web are third-party figures. In-feed ads need at least 540x960, at most 500 MB and at least 516 kbps. The safe area was measured by third parties from TikTok Ads Manager overlay files, and the bottom margin grows with caption length.
- **confidence:** official, checked 2026-09-30

Sources:

- <https://developers.tiktok.com/doc/content-posting-api-media-transfer-guide>
- <https://ads.tiktok.com/help/article/tiktok-auction-in-feed-ads?lang=en>
- <https://cadenus.io/resources/blog/tiktok-safe-zone/>
- <https://filesize.org/limits/tiktok/>

## youtube-video

**YouTube video** (video); also `youtube`, `yt`, `yt-video`

- **size:** 3840x2160 (16:9); also 2560x1440, 1920x1080, 1280x720
- **length:** up to 12 h; warns over 15 min: unverified accounts are limited to 15 min (verified ones: 12 h)
- **frame rate:** upload at the recorded rate: 24/25/30/48/50/60
- **audio:** optional
- **file:** at most 262144 MB
- **loudness:** -14 LUFS (measured by third parties; YouTube publishes no target)
- **formats:** mp4
- **codec:** MP4, no edit lists, moov atom at front. H.264 High Profile, progressive, 2 consecutive B-frames, closed GOP of half the frame rate, CABAC, VBR, 4:2:0, BT.709 SDR. SDR bitrates at 24-30 fps / 48-60 fps: 2160p 35-45 / 53-68 Mbps; 1440p 16 / 24; 1080p 8 / 12; 720p 5 / 7.5. HDR: 2160p 44-56 / 66-85; 1440p 20 / 30; 1080p 10 / 15. Audio: AAC-LC, Opus or Eclipsa Audio at 48 kHz; stereo 384 kbps (mono 128, 5.1 512).
- **notes:** Verified accounts can upload 256 GB or 12 h, whichever is less; unverified accounts are limited to 15 min. YouTube publishes no loudness target: ~-14 LUFS is measured by third parties, and YouTube only turns loud videos down.
- **confidence:** official, checked 2026-09-30

Sources:

- <https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/1722171?hl=en>
- <https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/71673?hl=en>
- <https://www.izotope.com/community/blog/mastering-for-streaming-platforms>
- <https://productionadvice.co.uk/stats-for-nerds/>

## youtube-short

**YouTube Short** (video); also `yt-short`, `shorts`

- **size:** 1080x1920 (9:16; 1:1 also counts as a Short); also 1080x1080; no other shape
- **length:** up to 3 min; warns over 1 min: YouTube blocks a Short over 1 min with any active Content ID claim, worldwide -- and a distributed song can carry one (the likely fix, unverified: whitelist your channel with your distributor)
- **frame rate:** same as youtube-video
- **audio:** optional
- **file:** at most 262144 MB
- **loudness:** -14 LUFS (measured by third parties; YouTube publishes no target)
- **safe area:** keep clear of top 192, bottom 480, left 0, right 108 px
- **formats:** mp4
- **codec:** Same encoding recommendations as youtube-video (1080p: 8 Mbps at 24-30 fps, 12 Mbps at 48-60 fps).
- **notes:** Square or vertical uploads up to 3 min become Shorts (previously 60 s): from 15 Oct 2024, but for Official Artist Channels only from 8 Dec 2025. To keep a music video of 3 min or less as long-form, upload it at 16:9 (YouTube's advice). Any Short over 1 min with any active Content ID claim is blocked globally; likely fix (unverified): whitelist your own channel with your distributor. Most licensed songs can be used for up to 90 s in a Short (some only 60 or 30 s). The safe area follows Google's Shorts-ads guidance: avoid the top 10%, bottom 25% and right 10%.
- **confidence:** official, checked 2026-09-30

Sources:

- <https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/15424877?hl=en>
- <https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/12779649?hl=en&co=GENIE.Platform%3DDesktop>

- <https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/1722171?hl=en>

## spotify-canvas

**Spotify Canvas** (video); also `canvas`

- **size:** 1080x1920 (9:16); also 720x1280; 720 to 1080 px wide; no other shape
- **length:** 3 s to 8 s
- **frame rate:** not published
- **audio:** none
- **file:** no limit published
- **formats:** mp4, jpg
- **codec:** H.264 MP4 with a video track only; third parties report embedded audio commonly causes upload failures. Spotify publishes no fps or file-size limit (the '8 MB' figure is third-party and unverified).
- **notes:** Spotify's wording 'Between 720px - 1080px tall' does not work literally at 9:16. It is usually read as the short edge, i.e. 720x1280 to 1080x1920. The Canvas loops in Now Playing, phone screens may crop the edges, and UI covers the top and bottom (no pixel margins published). Avoid talking, singing or rapping, rapid cuts and intense flashing. Not allowed: URLs or ticket links, follow/like prompts, social handles, brand or Spotify logos, product promos, contests, or unrelated text. Explicit content must be marked. Upload through Spotify for Artists. The Canvas is silent: the track it loops over plays at Spotify's normalisation, -14 LUFS by default (Loud -11, Quiet -19), from a master at or below -1 dBTP.
- **confidence:** official, checked 2026-09-30

Sources:

- <https://support.spotify.com/us/artists/article/canvas-content-policy/>
- <https://support.spotify.com/us/artists/article/fix-spotify-canvas-upload-error/>

## spotify-cover

**Spotify cover** (image)

- **size:** 3000x3000 (1:1); each side 640 to 10000 px; no other shape
- **audio:** none
- **file:** no limit published
- **formats:** jpg, png, tiff
- **codec:** Spotify: 640-10000 px per side, lossless-encoded TIFF/PNG/JPG, sRGB 24-bit with the colour profile applied (no embedded profile or orientation metadata), no upscaling.
- **notes:** Cover art reaches Spotify through a distributor, whose limits are stricter: 3000x3000 satisfies Spotify, Apple (3000 recommended) and every distributor in distributor-cover. Spotify normalises to -14 LUFS by default (Loud -11, Quiet -19; ITU-R BS.1770). Keep masters at or below -1 dBTP, or -2 dBTP if louder than -14 LUFS. Album playback keeps album gain; the limiter applies only in Loud mode.
- **confidence:** official, checked 2026-09-30

Sources:

- <https://support.spotify.com/us/artists/article/cover-art-requirements/>
- <https://support.spotify.com/us/artists/article/loudness-normalization/>

## distributor-cover

**Distributor cover** (image); also `distributor`, `distrokid`, `tunecore`, `cd-baby`, `amuse`, `unitedmasters`, `landr`, `soundcloud-distribution`

- **size:** 3000x3000 (1:1); each side exactly 3000 px; no other shape
- **audio:** none
- **file:** at most 10 MB
- **formats:** jpg
- **codec:** A square RGB JPEG of exactly 3000x3000 px, under 10 MB, is the one file every distributor listed here takes: DistroKid 1000 px or more, JPG only, 3000 ideal; TuneCore 1600-3000, under 10 MB; CD Baby 1400-3000, under 25 MB; Amuse 1400-6000; LANDR 1500-6000; UnitedMasters 3000-6000; SoundCloud for Artists 3000 or more, at 300 dpi.
- **notes:** The cover a distributor sends to every store. Between them, they refuse: text other than the artist name and the title (some allow the label), and a title written twice, side by side in two languages (SoundCloud); URLs, QR codes, social handles, store or brand logos, prices, dates and references to a CD or other physical format; images you don't hold the rights to, stock photos and art reused across releases; blurry, pixelated, stretched, rotated or cropped art; a Parental Advisory label on a release not marked explicit. Read your own distributor's page before release day: they change.
- **confidence:** official, checked 2026-10-01

Sources:

- <https://support.distrokid.com/hc/en-us/articles/360013534334-What-Are-the-Requirements-for-Album-Artwork>
- <https://support.tunecore.com/hc/en-us/articles/115006685728-What-are-TuneCore-s-cover-art-formatting-requirements>
- <https://support.cdbaby.com/hc/en-us/articles/360037660592-Artwork-Requirements>
- <https://support.amuse.io/en/articles/107739-what-is-important-when-it-comes-to-artwork>

## apple-music-cover

**Apple Music cover** (image); also `apple-cover`

- **size:** 3000x3000 (1:1); each side at least 1400 px; no other shape
- **audio:** none
- **file:** no limit published
- **formats:** jpg, png
- **codec:** JPEG or PNG at 100% quality. 3000x3000 or larger recommended; 1400x1400 minimum.
- **notes:** Delivered through a distributor. Not allowed: URLs, logos, QR codes, references to competitors, pricing or upselling, audio-format claims (Atmos, lossless, 24-bit), references to physical packaging or retailers, future release dates, misleading artist depictions, and low-quality, pixelated, misaligned or rotated art. The track plays with Sound Check, at ~-16 LUFS as third parties measure it; Apple publishes no number, and its only official figure is to 'leave at least 1 dB of headroom'.
- **confidence:** official, checked 2026-09-30

Sources:

- <https://itunespartner.apple.com/music/support/5215-digital-packaging-music>

## apple-music-motion-square

**Apple Music motion art, square** (video); also `apple-motion-square`

- **size:** 3840x3840 (1:1); no other shape
- **length:** 8 s to 35 s
- **frame rate:** 23.976, 24, 25, 29.97 or 30
- **audio:** none
- **file:** no limit published
- **formats:** mov, mp4
- **codec:** Apple ProRes 4444, 422 HQ, 422 or 422 LT in .mov, or H.264 in .mp4 at 45-100 Mbps. Rec.709 or sRGB, square pixels. Deliver without an audio track.
- **notes:** Shown on Mac, iPad and TV. Must loop seamlessly, and the first frame must match the cover. Not allowed: drop or hold frames, multiple edits, frame borders, frenetic flashing, a Parental Advisory logo, or static stills. Can only be delivered by a distributor or Preferred Provider; Apple Music for Artists has no self-upload. Symphonic limits it to 8-20 s (at $50), and FUGA supports singles and albums only; ask yours before making one. Silent: the track plays with Sound Check, at ~-16 LUFS as third parties measure it (Apple publishes no number).

## apple-music-motion-tall

**Apple Music motion art, tall** (video); also `apple-motion-tall`

- **size:** 2048x2732 (3:4); no other shape
- **length:** 8 s to 35 s
- **frame rate:** 23.976, 24, 25, 29.97 or 30
- **audio:** none
- **file:** no limit published
- **formats:** mov, mp4
- **codec:** Same as apple-music-motion-square.
- **notes:** Shown on iPhone and Android. Must be full-frame 3:4, not a scaled-down 1:1 image. Text and key art must stay in Apple's safe area, clear of the notch, UI text, buttons and the bottom gradient; Apple publishes no pixel margins. Symphonic requires both files to be the same length. Silent: the track plays with Sound Check, at ~-16 LUFS as third parties measure it (Apple publishes no number).
- **confidence:** official, checked 2026-09-30

## soundcloud-artwork

**SoundCloud artwork** (image); also `sc-artwork`

- **size:** 800x800 (1:1); each side at least 800 px; no other shape
- **audio:** none
- **file:** at most 2 MB
- **formats:** jpg, png
- **codec:** At least 800x800 px and under 2 MB.
- **notes:** 800x800 is the minimum; a larger square works if it stays under 2 MB, so a 3000x3000 distribution master usually needs recompressing. SoundCloud says it applies loudness normalisation. It recommends masters at -14 LUFS integrated and at or below -1 dBTP (-2 dBTP if louder). It streams Ogg/Vorbis and AAC.
- **confidence:** official, checked 2026-09-30

Sources:

- <https://help.soundcloud.com/hc/en-us/articles/46022345620123-Edit-and-customize-your-tracks>
- <https://help.soundcloud.com/hc/en-us/articles/360053660014-Will-SoundCloud-play-my-track-at-the-level-it-s-mastered>

## soundcloud-header

**SoundCloud header** (image); also `sc-header`

- **size:** 2480x520 (62:13; ~4.77:1); at least 2480 px wide, at least 520 px tall
- **audio:** none
- **file:** at most 2 MB
- **formats:** jpg, png
- **codec:** Minimum 2480x520 px.
- **notes:** Avoid text in the header because 'it will be cropped on smaller screens'. Drag and zoom repositioning only works for images larger than 1240x260. No pixel safe area is published.
- **confidence:** official, checked 2026-09-30
